quickSummary: Peter Mitchell's chemiosmotic hypothesis explains ATP synthesis driven by a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane. Because the thylakoid membrane is permeable to Mg2+ and Cl-, the electrical potential collapses, making the 1000-fold pH gradient (lumen pH ~5.0 vs stroma pH ~8.0) the primary driver. Protons accumulate in the lumen from OEC photolysis and PQH2 oxidation, and are depleted from the stroma by FNR. Efflux of 4 H+ through the CF0 channel drives rotational synthesis of 1 ATP at the CF1 headpiece.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Lumen is acidic (pH ~5.0), Stroma is basic (pH ~8.0). 4 H+ flowing through CF0 channel synthesizes 1 ATP at CF1 headpiece.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THYLAKOID PROTON GRADIENT SOURCES
                                      │
         ┌────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                            ▼                            ▼
  WATER SPLITTING (OEC)        Q-CYCLE / PQH₂ OXIDATION      FNR NADP⁺ REDUCTION
  Accumulates $4\text{H}^+$    Translocates $4\text{H}^+$    Consumes $2\text{H}^+$ 
  directly inside Lumen.       from Stroma into Lumen.      from Stroma.
conceptBreakdown.content:
Proton translocation establishes a **Proton Motive Force ($\Delta p$)** across the thylakoid membrane:
$$\Delta p = \Delta \psi - \left( \frac{2.3 R T}{F} \right) \Delta \text{pH}$$
Because thylakoid membranes are permeable to counter-ions ($\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cl}^-$), $\Delta \psi$ collapses, making the **$\Delta \text{pH}$ chemical gradient ($\text{pH}_{\text{stroma}} \approx 8.0$ vs $\text{pH}_{\text{lumen}} \approx 5.0$, a $1000$-fold difference)** the primary driving force.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 CF₀-CF₁ ATP Synthase Architecture
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 CF₀-CF₁ ATP Synthase Architecture
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CHEMIOSMOTIC THYLAKOID MEMBRANE
                        
     STROMA (pH ~8.0) ──► Low [H⁺]
     ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ (Thylakoid Membrane)
     LUMEN  (pH ~5.0) ──► High [H⁺]  ──► Translocates through CF₀ Channel ──► CF₁ Headpiece
                                                                                 │
     ADP + P_i ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────► ATP
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **$\text{CF}_0$ Subunit**: Hydrophobic transmembrane base consisting of a $c$-subunit oligomeric ring functioning as the proton translocating channel.
• **$\text{CF}_1$ Subunit**: Hydrophilic stroma-protruding catalytic headpiece with an $\alpha_3\beta_3$ hexamer that binds $\text{ADP} + \text{P}_i$.
• **Stoichiometric Ratio**: The passive efflux of **$4\text{ H}^+$ ions from lumen to stroma** through $\text{CF}_0$ induces rotational conformational changes in $\text{CF}_1$, synthesizing **$1\text{ molecule of ATP}$**.
